bug_semantics: UploadSet.save() accepted a caller-supplied name, split any slash-containing name into an unsanitized folder and basename, validated only the original uploaded file's extension, then replaced the validated basename with the attacker-controlled name and joined the unsanitized folder beneath the upload destination without a containment check. An attacker who could influence name could submit an allowed upload such as a JPEG while naming it ../templates/rce.html, causing an otherwise-disallowed template file to be written outside the upload directory; rendering that template could execute attacker-controlled Jinja expressions as SSTI/RCE.
flaw_origin: Commit 45b77b49476999bf824f987f17d013c218b8f9ee moved the file_allowed(storage, basename) check from after the name override to before it. That atomic regression completed the critical exploit chain by allowing an allowed source extension to authorize a different attacker-selected extension, on top of the already-existing unsanitized folder/name path join. Its immediate parent bb79c1def3a0940f929bc2cc0038047b36b9b2d8 checked the final overridden basename and therefore rejected the disallowed template extension used by this chain.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author is shrimpdede <feng.love.happy@163.com>, committer is GitHub <noreply@github.com>, and the message 'call file_allowed before basename changed (#15)' has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer; neither identity is an AI bot
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-27641 is PUBLISHED and identifies jugmac00/flask-reuploaded versions < 1.5.0 as affected; its CNA description states that path traversal plus extension bypass permits arbitrary file write and SSTI RCE and that 1.5.0 is patched: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-27641

The first-party GitHub advisory names the unsafe user-controlled name parameter, the < 1.5.0 affected range, 1.5.0 as patched, PR #180, and d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288: https://github.com/jugmac00/flask-reuploaded/security/advisories/GHSA-65mp-fq8v-56jr

git show 45b77b49476999bf824f987f17d013c218b8f9ee -- flask_uploads.py shows the sole causal code change: file_allowed(storage, basename) moved above the caller-controlled name assignment at lines 408-417, so validation applies to the uploaded filename rather than the final saved filename.

git show bb79c1def3a0940f929bc2cc0038047b36b9b2d8:flask_uploads.py lines 405-427 verifies the immediate parent split slash-containing name, applied the name override, and only then called file_allowed on that final basename; the extension-bypass-to-arbitrary-write chain is absent in the parent tree.

git cat-file -p 45b77b49476999bf824f987f17d013c218b8f9ee verifies one parent bb79c1def3a0940f929bc2cc0038047b36b9b2d8, human author shrimpdede, GitHub platform committer, and no AI authorship/co-authorship trailer. The one-parent commit directly contains the atomic validation-order regression; no squash-member decomposition is required.

git show d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 shows the direct fix in src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py: secure_filename() sanitization for name/folder, extension re-validation after name override, and realpath containment before storage.save(). Its parent 9e813e919c4f8d9ef17c7fe8ecc0c2efa8fee118 lacks all three protections.

PR #180 head be3f8c03d74ebeb2046e95b944c74895f44b0cca has the same tree as d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288, confirming d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 is the landed direct fix: https://github.com/jugmac00/flask-reuploaded/pull/180

Release topology is consistent: git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms BIC 45b77b49476999bf824f987f17d013c218b8f9ee precedes release 1.4.0 commit 0b050952856ed28b1d5f534c951c07bf7dabbeff, while fix d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 precedes release 1.5.0 commit ae31c3f91da40b465ca5e8f57d93f063b4553e23; pyproject.toml at the latter declares version 1.5.0.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and the official CVE remains published. Historical diff search shows that earlier code validated the final basename after any name override. The smallest commit that created the advisory's critical combined mechanism is 45b77b49476999bf824f987f17d013c218b8f9ee: it moved validation before the override, allowing an approved source file to authorize an attacker-selected disallowed template extension, while the existing unsanitized folder split and path join supplied traversal. Direct inspection of immediate parent bb79c1def3a0940f929bc2cc0038047b36b9b2d8 proves that combined mechanism absent there. Commit d64c6b2f71cb73734fc38baa0e3e156926361288 reverses the validation-order flaw and adds sanitization and containment; release ancestry places it in 1.5.0, matching the advisory boundary. AI attribution is decided only from the BIC object: it has a human author, a GitHub platform committer, and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
